clue.text: Meeting is annoyed by an African premier speaking

parts.note: cross means annoyed or irritated

indicators.note: speaking signals that the premier's name is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Cecil Rhodes was premier of the Cape Colony in southern Africa

explanation.surface: A meeting has left someone irritated by a speech from an African head of government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speaking' turns RHODES into its sound-alike ROADS. 'Meeting' is a noun here: a place where ways meet.
explanation.definitionFit: A junction where two roads cross is a meeting point of routes, so the noun fits.

clue.text: Band at wedding, exactly in tune, sound the real thing

parts.note: a wedding ring is a band of gold
true describes a note at exactly the right pitch

explanation.surface: The wedding band plays perfectly in tune and sounds authentic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' is a group of musicians on the surface, but a finger ring here.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a statement that seems genuine is said to have an authentic ring.

clue.text: Baronet is elevated by queen

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A baronet is raised to a higher rank by the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' turns IS upward to SI in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A baronet is addressed by the title used for knights, as in a formal honorific.

clue.text: Regret eating half of vegetables and Indian bread

indicators.note: eating means taking something in, so the piece goes inside

explanation.surface: Someone regrets a meal of vegetables with Indian flatbread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bread' is slang for money, not naan or chapati.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money, and this coin is India's currency unit.

clue.text: Robot with designer turning up

parts.note: and means together with

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Christian Dior was a French fashion designer

explanation.surface: A robot arrives together with a fashion designer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' looks like arriving, but it reverses DIOR to ROID.
explanation.definitionFit: A humanoid machine of science fiction is a kind of automaton.

clue.text: One always complaining merchant stores Bordeaux the wrong way up

indicators.note: stores means holds inside, so the wine goes within

parts.note: a seller is a merchant

indicators.note: the wrong way up in a down clue means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: Bordeaux is a French wine, and vin is French for wine

explanation.surface: A grumbling wine merchant keeps his Bordeaux upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way up' suits a down entry, where the French word for wine is read upwards; 'Bordeaux' stands for wine in general.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who whines and whimpers constantly is a perpetual moaner.

clue.text: Pleased with result after England is robbed of points

indicators.note: being robbed of something means losing it, so these letters are taken away from the country

parts.note: compass points: E for east and N for north, twice

explanation.surface: Someone is happy with the score after England's side drop points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' are compass points; removing E, N and N from ENGLAND leaves the answer. 'with result after' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: being pleased is being happy or delighted.

clue.text: Used coffee very much to give a rise in general feeling

parts.note: coffee grounds are what is left after brewing
well means very much, as in well worth it

explanation.surface: Spent coffee leaves give a great lift to public mood.
explanation.definitionFit: A surge of popular opinion or emotion is a build-up of public sentiment.

clue.text: Serve round tart to each one

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the serve goes around the pastry

parts.note: an ace is a serve in tennis that the opponent cannot touch
a tart is a kind of pie

explanation.surface: Someone serves a round tart to each guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serve' looks like a verb of dishing up, but it is a tennis term.
explanation.definitionFit: Each person getting a share means every individual gets one: per head.

clue.text: In time, roaming pride becomes fearless

indicators.note: roaming means wandering about, so the letters of pride wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Over time, a wandering pride of lions grows bold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roaming' looks like the lions' behaviour but tells you to scramble the word for the pack.
explanation.definitionFit: A direct synonym: someone intrepid shows no fear in the face of danger.

clue.text: One figure on a plane is famously representative

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a conic section is a curve drawn on a flat geometric plane

explanation.surface: A single passenger on an aircraft is held up as typical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' suggests an aircraft, but it is the flat surface of geometry, where conic sections such as ellipses are drawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Something iconic is widely recognised as a symbol standing for a whole type or era.

clue.text: Wife will have trouble with such conflict

definitions.text: Wife will have trouble with such
definitions.meaning: in Cockney rhyming slang, wife is 'trouble and', the word that rhymes completing the pair
a plain sense: bitter disagreement or fighting

explanation.surface: A wife foresees difficulty in a quarrel of this kind.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang, a London dialect, replaces a word with a rhyming phrase: 'trouble and strife' means wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A direct synonym: discord and fighting between people is conflict.

clue.text: What turns round over? It's nice bat, perhaps

indicators.note: turns round means the letters are spun into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A cricket question: what spins round in an over, and is it a nice bat?
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns round' rearranges OVER and ITS NICE together. 'bat, perhaps' is a definition by example: many bats feed on bugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Many bats eat bugs, so a bat is an example of a bug-eating animal.

clue.text: Too fussy concerning place to stay on the Riviera

parts.note: over can mean about or concerning, as in a row over money

parts.words: place to stay on the Riviera
parts.note: Nice is a resort city on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: A traveller is choosy about where to stay on the Mediterranean coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Being overly particular or fastidious is a dated sense of the compound adjective.

clue.text: Foreign figures that are just so full of themselves

definitions.text: Foreign figures that are just so full of themselves

parts.words: Foreign figures that are just so full of themselves
parts.note: nesting wooden figures from Russia each hold smaller copies of themselves, so are literally full of themselves

explanation.walkthrough: 'full of themselves' suggests vanity, but it is literal: each doll contains smaller ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Matryoshka sets are figurines from Russia, each housing a smaller replica inside.

clue.text: Gangster expands into light metal

explanation.walkthrough: The chemical symbol Al looks like the gangster's first name; expanded in full, the symbol names the element.
explanation.definitionFit: A lightweight silvery element widely used in cans and aircraft, symbol Al.

clue.text: Rise aloft endlessly to change part of the rigging

explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts ALOFT to ALOF; 'to change' rearranges it with RISE.
explanation.definitionFit: The forward sail on the foremast is one of the canvases a ship carries.

clue.text: Drift past bar, being highly vocal

indicators.note: past means coming after, so this piece follows the bar

explanation.walkthrough: 'Drift' looks like a verb of wandering, but it is the noun meaning gist.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer with the highest adult male voice is a being whose voice sits very high.

clue.text: Support for climbers is seen after report about mountaineer's end

indicators.note: end means the final letter of the word

explanation.definitionFit: A lattice frame holds up climbing plants such as roses or ivy in a garden.

clue.text: Shortly look at limiting leave for fairness

to quit is to leave

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' looks like 'soon' but means cut short; 'limiting' means enclosing; 'leave' is a verb, not time off.
explanation.definitionFit: Even-handed justice and impartiality are what the legal term denotes.

clue.text: A short joke sequence — one sees some hooters like this

definitions.text: one sees some hooters like this

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a quip is a witty remark or joke

explanation.surface: A series of gags prompts laughter, and some people honk along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooters' is British slang for noses, not car horns; a hooked nose is described this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooked like an eagle's beak, the adjective describes certain prominent noses.

clue.text: Everything in swamp is dead

parts.note: a fen is low marshy land
all means everything

explanation.surface: Everything in the marsh has died.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers killed in battle are called the fallen, so the word means killed or lifeless.

clue.text: Composer unknown in the end, not having succeeded

explanation.definitionFit: Gerald Finzi was a twentieth-century English writer of songs and choral music.
